details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). settings() bounds per-gate by max(2, 2 x jobs) where jobs = jobs_from(environ), the calling
process's RELAY_TEST_JOBS; read_setting also clamps the DEFAULT into that bound. The token kinds are index ranges
computed by each process from its own Settings, so two processes on one machine can disagree on R. The design's
bound "a slot holder always finds r of them not held as base (R = r x slots)" needs every process to compute the same
R. RELAY_TEST_JOBS=1 is a documented setting ("1 is the single process of run_unittest"; settings table "1: the run
never asks for extras"). The same split drift happens with a per-gate file above 2 x jobs for any process whose
RELAY_TEST_JOBS is lower than the gate's. Size: 15.
evidence: python3 settings for jobs 1..4 at 2 slots, 12 cpus:
Reproduction on a scratch RELAY_HOME (gate-slots/count 2): 4 shared held, gate A holds 4, then
gate B after 3 s: still waiting
failing_case: Pool of 12 (2 slots, per-gate default 4, so gate tokens 0..7, shared 8..11). All 4 shared tokens are held by lane runs,
gate A holds tokens 0..3. A lane starts `RELAY_TEST_JOBS=1 python3 tests/run_unittest.py tests.test_x` (or pytest with
that variable set). Its settings clamp per-gate to 2 x 1 = 2, so for it R = 4 and token-4 is "shared": it takes token-4
as its base at once instead of waiting. Gate B, holding the second slot, then waits for token-4 until that lane run ends
(a lane pytest session: up to ~1600 s), not "at most one class" as design rule 1 promises.
Now: lane gets token-4 with no wait; gate B still waiting after 3 s.
Should: the lane waits for a shared token (8..11); gate B gets 4..7 at once.
fix_hint: Make the split a machine-wide fact: bound per-gate by a constant (2 .. 2 x DEFAULT_JOBS, i.e. 2..8), not by the
caller's RELAY_TEST_JOBS, and drop the jobs argument from settings() for the partition (RELAY_TEST_JOBS stays the
per-run worker ceiling only). Add the pass-case tests to tests/test_relay_tokens.py.

- With that same state, take_base(h, s, GATE, 4) returns 4 tokens within 1 s.
- per-gate file "99" still comes back clamped to the upper bound with a note (today 8), the same value for every process.
- per-gate file "1" still comes back as 2 with a note.
